subject: Alpha team redistribution and individual care paths
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Alpha team redistribution and individual care paths

Hi Lauren and Marcus —

Following last week's leadership forum, I've sketched a focused proposal to rebalance the Alpha team across two product pods (Edge Serving & Optimize). The goals are to reduce single-team bus risk, improve cross-pod feature ownership, and create clearer promotion/mentorship lanes. This note is intentionally concise; attached is the role matrix and proposed individual care-path templates.

High-level (proposal):
- Move three senior engineers (Eng2, Eng3, Eng5) to Edge Serving for the next 6 months to accelerate latency projects.
- Reassign two mid-level ICs (Eng7, Eng8) to Optimize to lead performance tooling workstreams.
- Keep Eng1 (lead) in Alpha to own backlog continuity and support ramp.

Key constraints / sensitive points:
- Several people are mid-cycle in performance reviews; we should avoid surprises in compensation/ratings tied to move.
- Some engineers have expressed other role preferences; we need private 1:1s before any broad comms.
- Timing should align with the next review window (Jan) and avoid immediate promotion freezes.

Asks:
1) HR (Mina) — please confirm feasibility for mid-cycle redeployments and guidance on messaging for review impact.
2) Lauren — recommendation on manager-of-record during 6-month rotations and compensation handling.
3) Marcus/Kim — any objections on technical fit or critical projects that prevent specific moves.

I propose a staggered timeline: confidential 1:1s next week, manager-level alignment the week after, then a leadership sign-off by Nov 20. If we get buy-in, I can draft manager and all-hands comms.

Attachments: alpha_team_role_matrix.xlsx, care_path_templates.pdf

—
Jonas Weber
Head of Compute Platforms
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:35:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Alpha team redistribution and individual care paths

Thanks Jonas — good, pragmatic start. A couple of quick notes:

- Manager-of-record: I recommend Marcus remain manager-of-record for Eng2 and Eng3 while they rotate (dotted-line to Edge PM). This keeps performance consistency.
- Review timing: mid-cycle moves are okay if we treat the rotation as a stretch assignment and keep current review scorebases intact for this cycle. We can add an addendum in the review notes to reflect the rotation.
- Communication: prefer manager-first 1:1s, followed by a short private email to the team leads (no all-hands until everyone acknowledged).

I flagged two calendar conflicts in the matrix (Eng5 has planned leave week of Nov 23). We should avoid starting with them.

I'll review the care_path_templates and suggest language for the manager comms. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync with you and Mina today.

-L

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:12:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Alpha team redistribution and individual care paths

Appreciate the heads-up. A few HR guardrails and recommended edits: 

1) Performance & comp: We cannot change effective review windows or rebase compensation mid-cycle without a formal calibration note. The approach Lauren outlined (marking rotations as "stretch assignments" and preserving scores for the current cycle) is acceptable and reduces legal/expectation risk.

2) Documentation: please use the care_path_templates.pdf to record each 1:1 outcome. That file has required fields for impact, timeline, manager expectations, and support resources. All templates must be stored in a private HR folder (link provided).

3) Sensitive comms: For impacted individuals, managers must use the following cadence: 1) private 1:1, 2) shared transition plan with the receiving manager, 3) update to direct-report roster (no distribution outside the two pods until sign-off).

4) Outplacement / support: if any person prefers not to rotate and requests a separation, please loop people-ops-consultant@talentbridge.com (cc'd). We should avoid surprises to candidates or hiring partners.

I can join the 20-min sync this afternoon; propose 3:30pm PT.

Mina Haddad
Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Quick technical check: Eng7 has a critical dependency on the retraining infra scheduled Nov 29–Dec 3. If Eng7 moves the week of Nov 15, I need to confirm coverage or shift that infra work. I can reassign a contractor temporarily, but want to avoid unplanned delays.

On manager-of-record: fine with the dotted-line approach; I'll accept manager responsibility for review context and ensure feedback flows into their review doc.

No objections to the overall plan provided we respect the leave week for Eng5 and keep the 1:1-first cadence.

-Marcus

- Timeline: confidential manager 1:1s Nov 16–18; managers align Nov 19; leadership sign-off by Nov 20.
- Changes: Eng2, Eng3 -> Edge (dotted-line for Marcus); Eng7, Eng8 -> Optimize (start Dec 1); Eng5 postponed until Dec 15 due to leave.
- HR actions (Mina): prepare review addendum templates and create private folder for care-path artifacts.
- Comms owner: Kim will draft manager comms; Jonas will draft the short leadership note.
